summary: Alert Volume Trend Endpoint: GET /api/alerts/trends?days=N (default 7, 1-90) returns one bucket per UTC calendar day for the last N days (oldest first) with total count and per-severity counts, zero-filled; invalid days returns 400 ValidationProblemDetails.

acceptance_criteria.text: GET /api/alerts/trends returns 200 with one bucket per UTC calendar day, each with date, total count and a count per severity (Low, Medium, High, Critical).
When 'days' is omitted it defaults to 7 (response contains 7 buckets); 'days=N' returns exactly N buckets covering the last N UTC days including today.
Days and severities with no alerts are present with count 0 (total = sum of the four severity counts).
Severity count shape/ordering reuses the summary endpoint convention (AlertSeverityCountsResponse: Low, Medium, High, Critical; enums serialized as strings).
'days' below 1 or above 90 (e.g. 0, -1, 91) returns 400 with ValidationProblemDetails; boundary values 1 and 90 are accepted.
Non-numeric 'days' (e.g. 'abc') returns 400 with ValidationProblemDetails, consistent with existing query validation.

scope_anchors: GET /api/alerts/trends -> AlertsController (new action; route must not collide with '{id:int}')
IAlertService / AlertManagementService (new GetTrendsAsync; TimeProvider for 'today' UTC; zero-fill + ordering)
IAlertRepository + AlertRepository (new grouped count by CreatedDate.Date + Severity over CreatedDate >= startUtc)
AlertQueryRequest (existing [Range]/[FromQuery] DataAnnotations validation pattern) -> new AlertTrendsQueryRequest
constraints: Scope exceeds the 5-source-file cap deliberately (8 files incl. 2 new DTOs): story crosses Controller, Service, Repository interface/impl, DTOs and constants.
Keep layering Controller -> IAlertService -> IAlertRepository -> AlertDbContext; controller stays HTTP-only; entities never leave the service layer.

Validation via DataAnnotations on a [FromQuery] request DTO ([Range(1, MaxTrendDays)], default 7 from AlertConstants), mirroring AlertQueryRequest; [ApiController] automatic 400 yields ValidationProblemDetails for both out-of-range and non-numeric values. Do not add custom error formats; no hardcoded 7/90 outside AlertConstants.
Declare the 'trends' action as [HttpGet("trends")] with ProducesResponseType 200 and ValidationProblemDetails 400; literal route takes precedence over '{id:int}'.
Use TimeProvider (already injected) for 'today' (UTC date); window start = today(UTC) - (N-1) days at 00:00; repository filters CreatedDate >= startUtc.

Repository must aggregate in the database (GroupBy CreatedDate.Date + Severity, parameterized EF, AsNoTracking, no raw SQL, no per-row materialization); service zero-fills missing days/severities and orders oldest first.

Response uses DTOs only; severity counts reuse AlertSeverityCountsResponse (Low, Medium, High, Critical order); bucket date serialized as an ISO date (yyyy-MM-dd) or UTC DateTime per DTO convention - pick one and keep it consistent in tests.
Counts include all alerts regardless of IsActive (story says 'alert-creation counts'); no schema change or migration expected.
coverage_goals: AC1-AC7 each covered by at least one passing test: service zero-fill/ordering/default window/boundary days; repository grouping by UTC day + severity incl. window start boundary; request DTO Range validation (0, 1, 90, 91, default 7); controller 200 mapping.
missing_facts: Response contract not specified: assumed a JSON array of buckets { date, totalCount, severityCounts { low, medium, high, critical } } (array vs. wrapper object with 'days').
unresolved_questions: Assumed trends count all alerts (active and inactive) by CreatedDate.
Non-numeric 'days' 400 relies on [ApiController] model-binding failure (not unit-testable via Validator); verify via a WebApplicationFactory test only if /unit-testing deems it necessary.
Window includes today (partial day) and the previous N-1 days.
